newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE sees Australia copper output up 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: ABARE sees Australia copper output up 15 percent.

text.p: Australian copper mine output is forecast to rise 15 percent in 1997/98 to 595,000 tonnes following an 8.3 percent rise in 1996/97 year, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said on Tuesday.

Production of refined copper should rise nearly 20 percent in 1997/98 (July/June) to 370,000 tonnes after rising six percent in 1996/97 owing to expansions at WMC Ltd's Olympic Dam project in South Australia and at MIM Holdings Ltd's Townsville refinery in Queensland, ABARE said.

ABARE, the Australian government's main commodities forecaster, said in its June quarterly report that exports of refined copper were expected to jump 51 percent to 205,000 tonnes in 1997/98 from 135,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
The forecasts are largely in line with previous estimates made by ABARE in March.

ABARE said it expected average world copper prices to rise 6.1 percent in calendar 1997 from 1996 to US$2,435 a tonne (US$1.10 a pound). "Given the still relatively low stocks expected to prevail over the remainder of the year (calendar 1996), prices can be expected to remain volatile," ABARE said.

However, the agency said copper prices should fall 10 percent in 1998 to average US$2,200 a tonne (US$1.00 a pound) as increased supplies from new mines and smelters more than offset continuing strong global consumption growth.
ABARE said it expected world consumption of copper to grow 3.3 percent in 1997 over 1996 to 12.7 million tonnes.

The forecast rise reflected expectations of moderate growth in the industrial production in OECD countries, particularly the major economies in Western Europe and the United States as well as industrial growth in parts of Asia, it said.

"In Asia generally, continuing growth in construction industries associated with rapid infrastructure development and the growth of copper-intensive manufacturing, such as electronics and motor vehicles, are expected to be the driving forces in increased consumption," ABARE said.
Australia's export earnings from copper are forecast to rise to A$1.24 billion in 1997/98, up 29.5 percent from A$958 million the previous year, ABARE figures show.
